title: A King's Book of Joy
body: In 1283, King Alfonso of Spain was going through a very difficult time because his own son had rebelled against him. During a brief moment of peace, the king decided to create a beautiful book about games. He hoped that indoor games like chess would bring happiness and comfort to people who were sick, trapped, or lonely at home.

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a sad king named Alfonso faced a rebellion led by his own son. During a quiet moment of peace, he decided to paint and write a magnificent book all about indoor games. He hoped that the magic of chess would bring a little warmth and comfort to those who were feeling lonely or unwell in their homes.
variants.luca: Imagine your own family turning against you in a battle for the throne! That is exactly what happened to King Alfonso, but he did not give up. In a quick break from the fighting, he launched a brilliant plan to create a master guidebook of games. He wanted chess to be a secret weapon of joy for anyone trapped inside or fighting a tough illness.

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
